newsitem.title: UK: UK Channel 5 plans tuning promotion push.
newsitem.headline: UK Channel 5 plans tuning promotion push.

text.p: Channel 5 will use the screening of the Poland-England soccer match to urge more viewers to tune in their TV sets to its signal, Pearson TV chief executive Greg Dyke said on Friday.
"At least 20 percent of those who can receive the signal have not tuned their televisions to pick it up," Dyke told reporters after the Pearson AGM.
Dyke said that one-off events such as the Poland-England World Cup tie on May 31 would be used to encourage viewers to tune in to the new service.
Pearson, one of the major shareholders in Channel 5, said in a statement that the station was reaching around 50 percent of UK viewers.
It hopes to boost terrestrial coverage to around 85 percent of the population by the end of the year. It has also secured satellite transmission to help fill in the gaps in its transmission aerials.
Dyke said that a number of homes would need new aerials to pick up Channel 5, which has a weaker broadcast signal than its four terrestrial rivals.
The other shareholders in Channel 5, launched on March 30, are United News & Media Plc, European broadcast group CLT-Ufa and U.S. investment firm Warburg Pincus.
